Your first native mod

Create Mods/PracticeHelper.lua. Return a Lua table with a unique name, description, and optional callbacks. The runtime scans the game’s top-level Mods folder at startup.

{
  "id": "PracticeHelper",
  "name": "Practice Helper",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Settings for my practice tools.",
  "enabled": true
}

Lifecycle and settings

An extension returns a Lua table with optional onWorldReady(api), onTick(api), and buildSettings(api, panel) callbacks. The tick callback runs about twice a second, including while the menu is closed. Wood calls these on the game thread. Failures are logged separately so other mods can continue.

return {
  buildSettings = function(api, panel)
    api.label(panel, "Practice Helper")
    api.button(panel, "Toggle helper", function()
      api.set("enabled", not api.get("enabled", true))
    end)
  end
}
APIPurpose
api.playerControllerThe active Unreal player controller
api.label(panel, text)Add a native text label
api.button(panel, text, callback)Add a native button
api.section(panel, title, description)Add a themed settings section
api.toggle(panel, label, value, callback)Add an On/Off control; the callback receives a boolean
api.slider(panel, label, min, max, step, value, callback, format)Add a bounded slider with keyboard-friendly adjustment buttons
api.input(panel, hint, initial)Add a native editable text field
api.refreshSettings()Rebuild the active settings page after a reset
api.get(key, default)Read a persisted setting
api.set(key, value)Save a primitive setting value
api.log(message)Write a runtime diagnostic

Persistent values are stored in .wood/<mod-id>.settings.ini. Use single-line primitive values. Mod IDs may contain letters, digits, and underscores.

Build Wood from source

The source repository includes the installer, standalone Lua mods, UE4SS runtime, tests, documentation site, and a Windows release workflow.

python -m pip install -r requirements-build.txt
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python scripts/build_release.py
python scripts/verify_distribution.py
python scripts/package_netlify.py

Build on Windows using Python 3.10. The build script verifies the pinned official UE4SS archive and produces release/WoodSetup.exe. No game binaries or assets belong in the source repository.
